answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must stake cryptographic collateral that is burned under superlinear cost scaling: registering $k$ identities requires burning $O(k^2)$ tokens. When malicious entities embark on an exploit voyage, this quadratic penalty turns a fragile oasis into an economic sinkhole. Coordinated spamming triggers a devastating collateral ripple across all linked agents, making large-scale spoofing mathematically unviable.
